page: Amazon Web Services m6a.24xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by the AWS Nitro System. It runs on AMD EPYC 7R13 processors featuring 48 physical cores and 96 virtual CPUs with dedicated allocation. The CPU architecture is x86_64, capable of reaching clock frequencies up to 3.6 GHz, complemented by 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity stands at 384.0 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio at 4.0 GB per vCPU. Networking throughput delivers a baseline bandwidth of 38 Gbps. There is no bundled local storage or integrated hardware accelerator GPU present on this server configuration.

Benchmark analysis shows strong multi-threaded performance driven by its 96-thread core count. The instance achieves a top-tier stress-ng multi-core metric of 143,441.36 and top-tier PassMark CPU encryption score of 110,483.6, bolstered by dedicated hardware cryptography features like AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. Parallelized execution is further highlighted by a Geekbench ray tracing score of 90,198.0 and Clang compilation result of 55,230.0. In-memory operations show high efficiency, recording 90.99 million Redis SET operations per second and cached memory bandwidth of 6,034.75 GB/sec.

Single-core performance presents a modest tradeoff, with Geekbench single-core and single-threaded gzip compression remaining in the middle tier. Uncached memory read and write bandwidths similarly register average ratings at 133.81 GB/sec and 64.84 GB/sec, indicating that workloads are best structured to leverage multi-threaded CPU parallelization rather than raw single-core execution speed. Because instances in the AMD EPYC family deliver competitive resource density, this server offers efficient compute scaling for dense horizontally scaled platforms.

Amazon Web Services m6a.24xlarge is well aligned for large-scale enterprise applications, high-concurrency microservices, multi-threaded code compilation suites, relational database clusters requiring external network storage, and in-memory caches. It is also suitable for small-to-medium CPU-based LLM inference tasks, generating 300.69 tokens/sec for 135M parameter models.
description: Amazon Web Services m6a.24xlarge is a general-purpose, Nitro-powered instance driven by AMD EPYC 7R13 processors on the x86_64 architecture. Equipped with 48 physical cores, 96 dedicated vCPUs, and 384.0 GB of DDR4 memory, it establishes a balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio. Network capacity is supported by a 38 Gbps baseline, without bundled local storage or discrete GPU hardware. Benchmark evaluations reveal top-tier multi-core computational throughput, highlighted by strong results in stress-ng multi-core testing, AES encryption, and parallelized Clang compilation, alongside in-memory performance exceeding 90 million Redis SET operations per second. While single-thread operations and uncached memory bandwidth fall in the middle tier, the high thread count and large memory footprint deliver robust multi-threaded compute efficiency. This configuration fits distributed caching, high-traffic web backends, CI/CD compilation pipelines, and database servers leveraging decoupled remote storage.
